PM Circle Design Guidelines

Typography, spacing, colour, and reusable interface patterns for updating the PM Circle website.

Typography

Inter is the primary UI typeface. Use the existing Inter assets or self-host Inter as WOFF2 with font-display: swap. Use the variable font when available. With static fonts, load 400, 600 and 700, and align intermediate weights to the closest available weight. The HTML guide embeds the same Inter faces used in the prototype. The reusable stylesheet uses system UI fonts as fallback. Use lang="bn" for Bangla content and add a Bangla-capable font such as Noto Sans Bengali if the website introduces Bangla UI copy.

Live type specimens

The values beside each sample reflect its computed CSS at the current window width. Focus, hover or tap the type information to inspect the exact values. Inter is embedded at 400, 600 and 700. For other declared weights, the browser selects the closest available face.

Page title · H132–49.6px750 / 1.12One per page. Use the same banner treatment on catalog pages.

Set sizes in rem and preserve the browser’s default root size. Use sentence case for most labels and buttons. Use semantic heading levels in order and choose CSS for visual size. Keep running paragraphs around 60–75 characters per line where the layout allows. Allow text and controls to grow at 200% zoom.

Colour, spacing and layout

DecisionStandard
Spacing scale4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32 and 48px. Use 8–12px within related groups, 16px between cards, and 24–48px between sections.
Corner radius8px for inputs and buttons, 14px for cards, and 18px for dialogs or featured panels.
Page container1180px maximum width with 24px side gutters, reduced to 16px at 540px and below. Use the same container for banners, main content and footer content.
Full-width surfacesApply the background to the outer section. Place the inner content inside .pm-wrap. Use this structure for page banners, editorial notes and the footer.
Responsive gridThree columns above 850px, two down to 541px, one at 540px and below. Course list rows keep a compact thumbnail and flexible text. At narrow widths filters stack vertically.
Elevation and targetsUse borders by default. Use subtle shadow on interactive cards and a stronger shadow on dialogs. Keep buttons and form controls at least 44px high.

Use primary blue for the main next step. Use an outline button for alternatives and an underlined link for inline navigation. Use links to navigate and buttons for actions such as opening a popup or clearing filters. Keep access and availability separate. A simulator can be both Paid and in Preview.

Keep visible labels above inputs. Place the result count and Clear filters near the controls and update the count through a polite status region. Preserve filters while the user opens and closes a popup. For zero results, explain what happened and provide a way to clear filters. For required or invalid values, show a message beside the field and connect it with aria-describedby.

Page patterns

Page or flowContent order and behaviour
Shared header and footerKeep the PM Circle brand, familiar destinations and account actions in the same order across pages. Collapse navigation into an accessible menu on small screens. Group footer links by purpose. Use the dark footer palette and light link text.
Public page bannerFull-width blue-tinted background. Inside the common container, place breadcrumb, H1 and short subtitle in that order. Use the same pattern for Browse Exam Simulators and Learn & Practice.
Learn & PracticeBanner, Find Your Starting Point panel, topic options, filters and course results, pagination, full-width editorial note, footer. Show thumbnail, level, access, title, description, duration where known, metrics and View details.
Browse Exam SimulatorsBanner, profile discount offer, filters, card grid, learner reviews and footer. Place the PMP feature panel after the first visible row if PMP is present. Each card has a photo, area, availability, access, title, summary and View details.
Simulator details popupTitle, status and access, summary, audience, practice topics and actions. Available simulators lead to How to purchase. Preview simulators link to Compare plans and explain their availability.
Starting Point popupShow one question at a time with visible progress, stacked answers and a separate action row. Keep prior answers when moving back. Recommend a real catalog course with a reason. Determine the next action from membership and course access.
TestimonialsShow three cards on desktop, two on tablet and one on small screens. Allow touch scrolling and keyboard-operable Previous and Next buttons. Keep Write a review visible beside the section heading when space allows.
Other website pagesReuse the same type scale, colour tokens, form labels, buttons and status styles in Community, account screens and learning dashboards. Tables and exam-taking tools can use denser layouts where their tasks require it.
Course access and member statePrimary action
GuestRegister to continue. Carry the intended course through the registration flow.
Signed in, free course or eligible Plus accessStart course. Open the learning entry point.
Signed in, paid course without entitlementView Plus membership. Return to the course after successful upgrade.

For production recommendations, constrain AI output to actual catalog IDs and use account data to verify membership and course entitlement. Provide a retry or manual browse option if a recommendation cannot be generated. Keep the quiz progress, chosen answers and recommendation readable independently of the AI response.

Developer handoff

Copy PM_Circle_Design_System.css into the project, load it after the legacy CSS during migration, and add class="pm" to the body or the region being upgraded. Components have a pm- prefix. The standalone guide embeds the same component CSS so you can open it directly.

<link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/css/PM_Circle_Design_System.css">
<body class="pm">
  <main>
    <section class="pm-banner">
      <div class="pm-wrap">
        <nav class="pm-breadcrumb" aria-label="Breadcrumb">…</nav>
        <h1>Learn &amp; Practice</h1>
        <p class="pm-lead">Find project management courses for your role.</p>
      </div>
    </section>
  </main>
</body>
  1. Map existing styles to tokens, then migrate shared navigation, typography and buttons. Audit broad legacy selectors such as dialog form and .card img during migration.
  2. Move catalog cards, filters and full-width notes onto the shared styles. Reuse one component and vary content through markup and modifier classes.
  3. Use native <dialog> with showModal(). Supply an accessible title, explicit Close, Escape support and focus restoration. Verify that long content scrolls inside the popup and can be submitted by keyboard.
  4. Verify at 320px, 540px, 768px, 1024px and 1440px, with 200% zoom and keyboard only. Check line wrapping, visible focus, 4.5:1 normal text contrast, 3:1 large text and meaningful UI contrast, and no horizontal overflow outside intentionally scrollable regions.
  5. Check loading, empty, error, disabled, selected, pending and success states. Test filters together, page navigation, and the guest, free and Plus paths. Use meaningful alt text where an image supplies information, and empty alt text for decorative thumbnails that repeat adjacent content.

How we develop our courses

PM Circle courses draw on decades of hands-on experience from project management professionals. Their judgment shapes what we teach, from the skills that matter on real projects to the decisions learners get to practise. We use AI to help turn that experience into clear explanations, realistic scenarios, and practical exercises. Our project management experts are responsible for the content and its quality.
